title: Why New Phones Feel Like Downgrades
description: AI-narrated commentary on why flagship smartphones sometimes feel worse each generation -- the business logic of tiered releases, feature-gating, and spec-sheet segmentation behind it.

beats.text: Every year a new flagship drops, and every year someone says it's a downgrade.
Sometimes that's true -- charging bricks vanish, headphone jacks disappear, storage tiers shrink.
But 'downgrade' rarely means the phone got worse to build.
It usually means a feature got moved behind a paywall or a pricier tier.
Companies call it segmentation -- give away less on the base model so the pro version feels worth it.
Camera specs get 'upgraded' on paper while real-world processing gets tuned down to save battery.
It's not a mistake. It's a spreadsheet decision dressed up as an innovation.
So next time a spec sheet feels smaller, ask who actually benefited from the cut.
